requiredFindings.title: Use the already bound C2PM-1 declaration and admission rules
requiredFindings.finding: Q2 is already resolved at the pinned product base. Its design-lock.json binds c2pm-1-r2/successor.json (SHA-256 f75f9cbb3561826d128ad1bbbcd7f179a31c0ef24614202eb68f27d7bd71b446) with ACCEPT-DESIGN-UNIT. That successor selects the signed top-level closureProtocolMajor, mandatory for every new C2a projection, with independent presence/analyzer-equality rechecks, exact integer copying, role-specific support and descriptor agreement. The base also contains the optional property and the shared analyzer mismatch check. Leaving the source open, suggesting compatibility as the source, and mapping all refusals generically to J1 rows 27/56 omits accepted admission and public-route duties.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Add C2PM-1 as authority/dependency. Carry its ordered projection predicates, exact role support, authenticated-source controls and origin-sensitive native route publication through the owning implementation units. Do not infer an absent declaration from compatibility.providerProtocol or treat the supporting body-reader implementation as full C2a admission.

requiredFindings.title: Keep retention a prerequisite of admitted closures and native contexts
requiredFindings.finding: Separating a pure descriptor calculation from delivery is reasonable, but item 7:430 requires every admitted closure to retain its manifest and whole tree. NE:1493-1499 explicitly requires both compiler and stdlib closures retained whole and re-admits their records before digest comparisons. Q1 recommends digest-only context minting with retention deferred, contradicting that requirement and the gating memo. LD5 also calls the pre-retention operation production admission, even though its output cannot yet satisfy admission.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Define C2a-1 output before retention as an unadmitted candidate/projection that cannot authorize a context, Plan or worker. Gate successful production closure/context admission on C2a-3 or equivalent lawful complete retained inputs, including the compiler and stdlib. The fixture generator may supply synthetic bytes, but must exercise the same retention checks. Preserve the delivery-owner gate; do not count C2a-1/2 alone as unblocking successful C2b-1 context admission. Keep unavailability handling subject to item 7's X-8 and the existing durable/ephemeral routes.

requiredFindings.title: Place admission completion within the pre-draw R10a/ER10a boundary
requiredFindings.finding: LD1 places C2a admission after R10a and leaves its placement as a precondition. M3-C r8:71 says item 7 admission has already run no later than R10a, before any analysis-attempt ExecutionId, and row 8 adds no admission. J1:394,406-411 and M3-D item 24 put R10a before R11/R12. A new platform/protocol/field admission failure discovered after that boundary cannot silently become row-8 admission.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: State that the trust reader runs first, D4 performs its excluded-form checks, and the relevant C2a admission checks finish as part of R10a/ER10a before that boundary returns and before handoff/draw. Distinguish later selection and selected-closure retention from pre-draw admission. Name the composition controls that prove ordering and unchanged reservation sets on refusal; do not move draws or reverify signatures in C2a.

requiredFindings.title: Make the size controls and work accounting implementable
requiredFindings.finding: The unconditional control that 100,000 files admit is not achievable through the proposed full descriptor identity path. The identity canonical encoder has MAX_BYTES = 4 MiB (crates/identity/src/canonical.rs:5,279); 100,000 Blob objects alone exceed that bound. The input manifest also caps all TreeCommitment entries, including directories and symlinks, at 100,000. A 100,001-file signed manifest therefore refuses before projection. LD10 additionally leaves ledger selection and costs unspecified, although projection allocates path/Blob records, orders them, validates and canonicalizes/hashes the descriptor; the existing body reader does not require entry order.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Separate the schema count predicate from feasible whole-record admission. Retain existing upstream/canonical limits and test their typed refusals, with a feasible positive boundary. Specify the production ledger/profile and pre-allocation costs for descriptor/path ownership, ordering and identity work, including exhaustion and aggregate calls. If an isolated count test uses constructed input beyond manifest admission, label it as such rather than claiming production admission. Do not promise unconditional schema-max admission or introduce an unreviewed larger cap.

requiredFindings.title: Complete the item-9 field-use owner matrix
requiredFindings.finding: Assigning C2-T12/13/13a collectively to C4a and H covers Plan/view legs but does not enumerate all fields and restrictions in item 9 and bound CRC-1/CRC-2. These include dependency/prepared import producer and adapter admission; syntax stage/scope/binding and CandidateProducerResultV1 provenance; host inventory origin/relation/binding restrictions; and the all-role cache-key prohibition. E3 has explicit E3-T13/T14 legs (syntax-e/PROPOSAL.md:710-711), while import admission has its own owner. A generic Plan/view assignment leaves these duties untracked.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Add a field/control-to-owner matrix covering all admitted and refused uses, including import admission (C3), syntax production (E3), Plan/stage/binding selection (C4a), view/fact/scope admission (H), candidate-result admission and cache-key admission at their actual owners. Explicitly retain CRC-2's mirror rule and the symbol-inventory and candidate-result exclusions. Keep these as named dependencies/owed controls rather than claiming C2a implements every consumer. X12d must still prove the same-core detector join, beyond the evaluator's existing kind/membership checks.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Make the selected-platform join explicit
nonBlockingObservations.observation: The catalog is a valid authenticated source for the platform spelling: recovery_catalog.rs:68-79 admits the four component platform tokens. State the closed association between the selected manifest os/arch row and its same-release artifact token, with a mismatch/missing-artifact control. Merely copying a signed token does not join it to the selected tree. Core inventory platform spellings are a different vocabulary and must not be copied here.

nonBlockingObservations.title: Record the existing vector and preserve a narrow fixture seam
nonBlockingObservations.observation: core_inventory.rs already has crc1_vector_core_role_closures and crc1_all_accepted_inventory_cases_preserve_members_and_distinct_ids (665-737), covering pinned role ids, raw-body digest, only-kind projection and distinctness. Name them instead of leaving their existence uncertain. A shared fixture module is reasonable, preserving existing bytes and the exact joint predicate; it must build valid role-scoped manifests, including the C2PM-1 declaration for new projections, and must retain the existing synthetic label and release source pin.
